Kuvitus: syksyinen iltapäivä järven rann: Illustration: an autumn afternoon by a lake. On the road in the foreground a red car pulls a small trailer loaded with firewood. The car and the trailer are joined by a drawbar. Behind the road there is a lake with forest on the far shore, and birches and spruces grow along the road.
Käsitekartta. Ylhäällä solmu voimakuvio: Concept map. At the top is the node free-body diagram first: choose the object, find the interactions, draw the free-body diagram, choose the axes and write the equations of motion. Three branches go down from it. Newton's laws: first law, sum F is zero when the velocity is constant; second law sum F = m a; third law F A B = − F B A. Forces: weight G = m g, kinetic friction F mu = mu N and static friction at most mu zero N, air resistance opposes the motion. Special cases: on a slope G x = m g sin alpha, connected bodies have an equation each, and at terminal velocity F v = G.
Kaksi kuvaa. Vasemmalla tilannekuva: muo: Two pictures. On the left a situation picture: a plastic sledge slides down a snowy slope to the left. The slope rises to the right at the angle alpha to the horizontal. Above the sledge a blue velocity arrow and an orange acceleration arrow point down the slope. On the right the free-body diagram of the sledge, the sledge as a rectangle tilted parallel to the slope: the weight G straight down from the centre, the normal force N from the bottom surface perpendicular to the slope and outwards, and kinetic friction F mu from the upper corner of the bottom surface up the slope. The components of the weight are drawn with dashed lines from the centre: G x down the slope and G y perpendicular to the slope, towards it. The component G y is as long as the normal force, and G x is clearly longer than the friction, so the sum of the forces points down the slope. The lengths of the arrows are to scale.
Kuvaaja: vaunun kiihtyvyys a vetävän voi: Graph: the acceleration a of the cart as a function of the pulling force F. Seven black points at forces 0.40–1.60 N. A rising straight line is fitted to the points and extended as a dashed line down to the horizontal axis. The line passes through the points (0.40 N; 0.19 m/s²) and (1.60 N; 1.60 m/s²); these two points on the line are circled. The line crosses the horizontal axis at about F = 0.24 N and does not pass through the origin.
